title: Hosea: betrothed again (Hosea 2:16–22)
hook: a broken marriage restored becomes a picture of God and Israel

segments.voice: Yesterday, Trei Asar: twelve short prophets bound on one scroll so none of them would get lost. Your line was small books, big voices. Whose quiet words did you hear twice? Today, the first voice on that scroll. Day eight hundred eighteen.

The first thing Hosea is asked to do is marry. He marries Gomer, and the marriage goes wrong. In the chapters that follow, the book speaks of a wife who goes after other lovers, and it doesn't look away from the hurt. There are children with names that sound like verdicts. There's anger, and accusation, and a house gone cold. A story could end there. This one doesn't. Somewhere in the middle of the second chapter, the voice changes, and a door opens in the wall.
screen: `A PROPHET IS TOLD TO MARRY.` → `THE MARRIAGE BREAKS.` → `THEN THE VOICE CHANGES.`

segments.voice: Hosea's marriage becomes a picture of God and Israel: a covenant like a wedding, a people who wandered after other gods, a love that's been wounded. And in chapter two, God speaks like a husband who wants to begin again. In the 1917 Jewish translation: "I will allure her, And bring her into the wilderness, And speak tenderly unto her." The wilderness. Not as punishment, but as the place where the first love began, after Egypt, before all the trouble. Go back to where it started, and speak gently there. The valley of Achor, a valley remembered for an old trouble, becomes, the text says, "a door of hope." Then a small, sharp change of names. The text says that on that day you will call me Ishi, my husband, and no more Baali. Baali can also mean my husband, but it echoes the name of the god Baal, and the next verse says the names of the Baalim will be taken out of her mouth. The relationship is to be personal again, not one more lord among lords. And then the vows. In the 1917 Jewish translation: "And I will betroth thee unto Me for ever; Yea, I will betroth thee unto Me in righteousness, and in justice, And in lovingkindness, and in compassion. And I will betroth thee unto Me in faithfulness." Betroth, three times. Not remarried, betrothed: back to the very beginning, as if engaged for the first time. And the gifts listed aren't jewelry. They're righteousness, justice, lovingkindness, compassion, faithfulness. Some Jews say these lines each weekday morning, while winding the strap of the tefillin around the finger, like a ring.
screen: `A MARRIAGE AS A PICTURE OF COVENANT.` · `BACK TO THE WILDERNESS, SPOKEN TO GENTLY.` · then, large: `I WILL BETROTH THEE UNTO ME FOR EVER.` · then: `SAID WHILE WINDING THE TEFILLIN STRAP.`

segments.voice: Today's practice is to renew one relationship. Sit, and let your breathing slow. Bring to mind one person you've drifted from, or grown used to. A partner, a parent, a friend, a sibling. Go back, in your mind, to the wilderness: to the beginning, when it was new. What did you first notice about them? What did you like? Hold that for a while. Then ask what one word from Hosea's list this relationship needs: justice, kindness, compassion or faithfulness. If you pray, you can say the betrothal line slowly. The bell holds the time.
Hosea. The prophet whose broken marriage becomes a picture of God and Israel, and who hears God promise to betroth the people again. Today's word.
Your line: betrothed again. Today, send the person you thought of one sentence from the beginning: a memory, a thank you, a thing you first loved about them. Day eight hundred eighteen.

screen: `DAY 818 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: HOSEA: TAKE WITH YOU WORDS.`

howItsDone: Jews who wear tefillin often recite Hosea 2:21–22 on weekday mornings while winding the tefillin strap around the middle finger, and the verses are part of the haftarah for the Torah portion Bamidbar.

myth: in Hosea, the broken marriage ends the story
chapter two turns, and God promises to betroth the people again.
the wilderness here is only a place of punishment
God says, I will allure her, bring her into the wilderness, and speak tenderly unto her.
the betrothal gifts are righteousness, justice, lovingkindness, compassion and faithfulness
no jewelry. the gifts are ways of keeping faith.

fork.setup: the marriage in Hosea has broken. in chapter two, what does God say comes next?
options: a new betrothal, as if from the beginning.
fork.reveal: God says, I will betroth thee unto Me for ever, three times over: a fresh start, not a patched one.

original.note: Hebrew: and I will betroth you to Me, the opening of the vows in Hosea 2:21.

trapdoor: what you thought: Hosea is only a book about a bad marriage.
what it means: the marriage becomes a picture of God and Israel, and ends in a new betrothal.
what a scholar hears: the verses said while winding the tefillin strap each weekday morning, with betroth three times over.
